title: C482/1476/2021 of SAHIL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Misc. Application No. 1476 of 2021
Sahil ......Petitioner
Versus

State of Uttarakhand and another ....Respondents
Present:
Mr. Mani Kumar, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. V.K. Jemini, Deputy Advocate General for the
State.
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.(Oral)
 Challenge in this petition is made to the order
dated 28.09.2021, passed in Special Sessions Trial No.
345 of 2020, State of Uttarakhand Vs. Sahil (for short,
"the case"). By the impugned order, an application filed
under Section 311 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 (for short, "the Code") by the petitioner for cross
examination of the victim has been rejected.
2. Facts necessary to decide the controversy are
in a very short compass. The petitioner is facing trial in a
case for the offences punishable under Sections 376 and
506 IPC and 5/6 of the Protection of Children From
Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for short, "the Act"). In the
case, 20.04.2021 was a date fixed for examination of the

2
victim. She was examined, but none appeared for her
cross examination and the court closed the opportunity
to cross examine the witness. The petitioner has enclosed
the statement of the victim recorded in the case on
24.04.2021 as Annexure 2. This statement also records
that, in fact, the petitioner is in the jail and through video
conferencing, he had joined the proceedings.
3. Thereafter, an application under Section 311
of the Code has been filed on behalf of the petitioner
seeking permission to cross examine PW1 the victim on
the ground that on 24.04.2021, the counsel representing
the petitioner had withdrawn his vakalatnama and
therefore, did not cross examine the witness.
Subsequently, new counsel was engaged, who insisted
the engagement of earlier counsel also. Thereafter, the
application was filed.
4. Learned court below observed that
deliberately the earlier counsel withdrew his vakalatnama
on the date when the victim was present in the court and
subsequently, he again engaged himself in the case.
While observing it, the application has been rejected.

3
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner would
submit that a fault was committed by counsel for the
petitioner, for which he should not be penalised.
7. In fact in the instant case, on 26.10.2021, the
Court had observed the manner in which the victim
under the Act has been allowed to leave the court without
her cross examination and while observing it, the court
issued notice to the counsel, who had withdrawn his
vakalatnama on the day, when victim was present in the
case for recording her evidence. The court observed as
hereunder:-
"This Court does not want to comment
now the way the victim was allowed to go from
the court without cross-examination the day
she appeared. The Court also does not want to
comment now as to what made Mr. Sarvesh
Babu, Counsel to again file vakalatnama for
the petitioner so as to move an application for
cross-examination of the victim. Before
examining this issue, this Court considers it
appropriate to issue notice to Advocate Mr.
Sarvesh Babu, Rudrapur.
Issue notice to Advocate Mr. Sarvesh
Babu. He shall his explanation on the
followings;

4
(i) The accused being in jail and the
matter being under the POCSO Act,
when the victim was present in the
court, why he did not cross-examine
the victim?
(ii) What were the circumstances under
which he filed an application for
withdrawing his vakalatnama?
He shall also file a copy of the withdrawal
application, which he has submitted in the
court below.
List on 11.11.2021.
Till then, the final judgment shall not be
pronounced in the case.
After considering the response submitted
by Mr. Sarvesh Babu, Advocate, if required, the
matter may be referred to Bar Council of the
State of Uttarakhand to enquire and examine
the issue."
8. Mr. Sarvesh Babu, the counsel has shown the
cause and stated that since he did not have documents
on that date, therefore, he had no option but to withdraw
his vakalatnama.
9. Today, before this Court, an affidavit has been
filed by Mr. Sarvesh Babu. He states that he had no
intention to postpone the cross examination of the victim.
In para 5, he writes as hereunder:-
"That the Present Applicant called the Pairokar
of the Case Many Times and Requested to Provide the
Records which was Provided by the Learned Trial
Court to the Accused Person, than the Reply was Made

5
by the Pairokar that in Sub-Jail Haldwani, the Jail
Authorities are Not Allowing/Permitting Any Person to
Meet with the Accused Person, Resultantly the
Document's was Not Handed Over by the Accused or
the Pairokar Of the Case."
10. Section 33 sub section (5) of the Act provides
that "the Special Court shall ensure that the child is
not called repeatedly to testify in the court."
11. A litigant may not be permitted to design the
course of justice. Cases should proceed as per law with
utmost speed. But, at the same time, interest of the
accused should not be prejudiced adversely, particularly,
when he is in the jail.
12. The petitioner in the case was in the jail, when
PW1 the victim was examined in the case on 24.04.2021.
On that date, vakalatnama was withdrawn by the
counsel representing the petitioner. Right course should
have been to engage another counsel at the expense of
the State, so that the petitioner may be represented and
be defended in the case pending against him. But, it was
not done.
13. Therefore, this Court is of the view that
without further discussing any other aspect of the

6
matter, the impugned order deserves to be set aside and
the petitioner should be afforded an opportunity to cross
examine PW1, the victim.
14. At the same time, this Court may also observe
that the counsel, who represented the accused,
particularly in the cases under the Act, has also a legal
obligation as provided under Section 33 (5) of the Act,
which mandates that the court shall see that a witness is
not called repeatedly to testify in the court. A counsel has
also an obligation to see that the victim is not harassed.
The Court had initially intended to consider the case of
Mr. Sarvesh Babu for referring the matter to the State
Bar Council, but, now on his behalf, it is argued that he
had no intention to harass the victim. Due to want of
document, he could not represent the petitioner. In his
supplementary affidavit, Mr. Sarvesh Babu has again
narrated that his act was not intentional nor deliberate,
while doing so he also tendered unconditional apology.
15. Having considered the affidavit and
supplementary affidavit filed by Mr. Sarvesh Babu, there
appears to be no reason to proceed against him. The
chapter with regard to Mr. Sarvesh Babu is closed.

7
16. In view of foregoing, this Court is of the view
that while setting aside the impugned order, the
petitioner should be allowed to cross examine PW1, the
victim.
17. The petition is allowed. The impugned order,
passed in the case is set aside.
18. The application filed by the petitioner under
Section 311 of the Code is allowed. The petitioner shall
be given one more opportunity to cross examine PW1, the
victim.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 22.11.2021
Jitendra
